question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j,k\}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j,k\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
